chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who dies and bequeaths a Hajj, so a man is given dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf, but he dies before performing Hajj, then the dirhams are given to another. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he died in the way or in Makkah before fulfilling its rituals, then it suffices for the first one.' I said: 'If he was afflicted with something that invalidates his Hajj until the Hajj of the next year becomes obligatory upon him, does it suffice for the first one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Because the hired one is responsible for the Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.حَجَّةٍ: A specific year's or instance of Hajj pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: Does a bequeathed Hajj count as fulfilled if the agent dies or has his Hajj invalidated before completion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the liability (zamanah) of the appointed agent (muwakkal) in Hajj al-Nafi'ah, establishing that the obligation is discharged for the deceased even if the agent dies or suffers invalidation requiring a make-up Hajj. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the agent bears the risk of performance, ensuring the deceased's debt to God is settled upon the initial appointment or completion of core rites, reflecting the principle of 'ease in religion' (taysir).

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who dies and bequeath with a Hajj. So Dirhams are given to a man to perform Hajj with on his behalf, but he dies before he performs Hajj. Then the Dirhams are given to someone else. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he died in the way, or in Makkah before he had fulfilled his rituals, so it would suffice from the first one’. I said, ‘Supposing he is involved with something which spoils his Hajj upon him until the Hajj of the next year comes to be (Obligatory) upon him, would it suffice him from the first one?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Is it because the hired one is responsible for the Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who dies and says in his will to perform al-Hajj on his behalf, and a man is given expenses of al-Hajj to perform al-Hajj on behalf of the deceased but he also dies before performing al-Hajj, then dirhams are given to someone else. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he dies on the way or in Makkah before completing the acts of al-Hajj, it is sufficient for the first deceased.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if he (one hired to perform al-Hajj) is involved in something that invalidates his al-Hajj which requires him to perform al-Hajj in future, is it sufficient for the first deceased?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is sufficient.’ I then asked, ‘Is it because a person on hire is responsible for al-Hajj?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, that is correct.’”
